key_insight: Geometry tokens from pretrained 3D models can be made materially useful for vision–language models by changing how they are fused and fine-tuned, enabling much better spatial reasoning in static scenes and dynamic videos.
problem_solved: Vision–language models underuse geometric cues when geometry tokens are naively appended and standard fine‑tuning is applied, limiting performance on tasks that require understanding relative positions, depth, occlusion and motion.
method: Extract compact geometry tokens from pretrained 3D foundation models (depth, point-cloud or mesh features) to represent scene geometry.
Introduce a geometry-aware fusion module that preserves geometric relationships and injects geometry into cross-modal attention (or feature modulation) rather than simple token concatenation.

Design geometry-centric training objectives and a targeted fine‑tuning schedule (e.g., alignment/contrastive losses, spatial completion or masked-geometry tasks) to ensure the VLM actually leverages geometric cues.
impact: Makes VLMs substantially more capable at spatial reasoning tasks (relative location, occlusion handling, motion grounding), which benefits applications in robotics, AR/VR, autonomous systems and video understanding by providing more reliable spatial grounding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image/video → geometry extractor (3D model) → geometry-aware fusion → VLM outputs (QA/relations) — annotated to show where geometry is injected.
Before vs after examples: paired visual QA or relation-prediction cases showing failures with naive fusion and corrected answers with the proposed method.
Attention/activation heatmaps: overlays that show increased model focus on geometric regions after geometry-aware fusion.
Performance snapshot: compact bar or radar chart illustrating relative improvements on representative spatial-reasoning benchmarks or qualitative metrics.
paper_title: Make Geometry Matter for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Shihua Zhang, Qiuhong Shen, Shizun Wang, Tianbo Pan, Xinchao Wang
